read: partial: abstract and sections 1-7 (introduction, related work, GSM1k construction and checks, results, analysis, discussion) in full; appendices A-F and J-L read or skimmed; the 50 example problems (appendix G), the extra plots and the reference list not read
venue_now: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (p.1 footnote: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, Track on Datasets and Benchmarks); arXiv 2405.00332v4 [cs.CL], 22 Nov 2024
what_it_is: GSM1k: 1,205 grade-school arithmetic word problems written from scratch by paid human annotators, without LLM help, to mirror GSM8k in style and difficulty, built to measure how far models' GSM8k scores reflect overfitting or contamination (p.1-4). Items passed three review layers (2,108 initial problems; 1,419 passed an independent second solve; 1,375 passed a quality audit; 1,205 kept after matching GSM8k's answer-magnitude distribution) (p.4-5). Human distinguishability and solve-rate tests show it is comparable to GSM8k (p.5). Many open and closed models are scored 5-shot on both sets: accuracy drops of up to 8 points, systematic overfitting in some families (Phi, Mistral) and minimal signs of it for frontier models (p.1, p.7-8, p.25).
size: 1,205 problems (p.2, p.5); about 60 open and closed models (62 rows in the standard-prompt results table by my count, p.25-26)
source_of_items: newly written by paid human annotators (Scale AI), shown three GSM8k examples per task and asked for novel problems of similar difficulty; no LLM used (p.3-4, p.19-20)
instances: static (a fixed set, kept private at the time of the paper) (p.3-4)
has_gold_traces: no: the released format is a question and an integer answer (p.19); annotators wrote resolution steps (p.20) but they are not part of the benchmark
evaluation: final answer: LM Evaluation Harness extracts the last number in the response and exact-matches it to the integer answer; 5 random GSM8k train examples as few-shot (p.6)
human_validation: Items: three review layers (manual review for correctness and level; an independent second solve with mismatches discarded; a quality audit) (p.4). Comparability: 19 annotators found the lone GSM1k question among five 21.83% of the time over 1,205 attempts (chance 20%); 14 annotators solved 4.36 +/- 1.11 GSM1k and 4.07 +/- 0.93 GSM8k problems in 15 minutes (p.5). Evaluator: a human answer-extraction ablation on a subset of models changed absolute scores but not the overfitting findings (p.6, appendix J p.39).
contamination_measures: private test set with human-only authorship (not released; release promised by June 2025 or when three open models reach 95%); GPT-NeoX-20B and GPT-2 solve-rate sanity check; log-likelihood analysis (p.3-5, p.8)

engtrace_use.sentence: Static test sets saturate (Ott et al., 2022; Akhtar et al., 2026) and leak into training data (Deng et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024), [...]
engtrace_use.explanation: GSM1k supports overfitting to GSM8k and gives suggestive but indirect evidence of leakage; it does not show that static sets leak into training data, and it says contamination is probably not the whole explanation. The evidence. (1) Accuracy on GSM1k is lower than on GSM8k for many models, by up to 8.0 points (Yi-6B-Chat, 43.7% to 35.7%; math-shepherd-mistral-7b-rl, 82.6% to 75.4%) (p.25), systematically for the Phi and Mistral families, and not for frontier models, which 'show minimal signs of overfitting' (p.1, p.3, p.7-8). (2) A correlation between a model's per-character log-likelihood of the GSM8k test set and its GSM8k-GSM1k gap: Spearman 0.36 (p = 0.03), Pearson r^2 0.26, Kendall tau 0.29 (p.8); the text reads it as 'partial memorization of the test set' (p.8) and the Figure 5 caption as suggesting that 'some of the GSM8k test set may have leaked into the model training data' (p.7). The paper then says 'data contamination is likely not the full story' (p.8): a heavily overfit model with low likelihood (Math-Shepherd-Mistral-7B-RL) and models with high likelihood but no overfitting (Llemma) are outliers (p.8-9); indirect routes are suggested, such as builders collecting data similar to the benchmark or selecting checkpoints on it (p.9); and training sets are not inspected ('impossible to know for certain without looking at the training set', p.8). The introduction and discussion are firmer than the analysis ('confirms the widespread suspicion', p.2; 'substantial evidence that many models have been contaminated', p.9). Overfit models still solve novel problems: Phi-2 solves over half of GSM1k (p.8).

suggested_wording: Static test sets saturate (Ott et al., 2022; Akhtar et al., 2026) and can leak into training data (Deng et al., 2024); on GSM1k, a fresh human-written set matched to GSM8k, some model families score up to 8 points lower than on GSM8k, which the authors read as partial memorisation (Zhang et al., 2024).
facts_to_cite: 1,205 problems written by human annotators without LLM help; 2,108 initial problems, 1,419 passed the independent second solve, 1,375 the quality audit, 1,205 kept after matching GSM8k's answer-magnitude distribution (p.2-5)
accuracy drops of up to 8 points: Yi-6B-Chat 43.7% on GSM8k against 35.7% on GSM1k; math-shepherd-mistral-7b-rl 82.6% against 75.4% (p.25)
systematic overfitting in the Phi and Mistral families; all frontier and close-to-frontier models perform similarly on both sets (p.7-8)
Spearman 0.36 (p = 0.03), Pearson r^2 0.26, Kendall tau 0.29 between the log-likelihood of the GSM8k test set and the GSM8k-GSM1k gap (p.8)
'data contamination is likely not the full story'; outliers and indirect routes (p.8-9)
overfit models still reason: Phi-2 loses 6 points yet solves over half of GSM1k (p.8)
comparability checks: human distinguishability 21.83% against 20% chance; human solve rates 4.36 against 4.07 problems in 15 minutes (p.5)
release policy: GSM1k not released; release promised by June 2025 or when three open models of different lineages reach 95% accuracy (p.3-4)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: the motivation (contamination of static public sets) and a held-out private set as the remedy. Lacks: generated instances (a fixed human-written set), step-level scoring, gold traces, an engineering domain, and any validated scorer beyond a human answer-extraction ablation. The positioning claim still holds. Contrast: GSM1k is a fixed private set that had to be sent to API providers for evaluation (p.4); a seeded generator, as in EngTrace, can be re-drawn if a set leaks (inference).
notes: (1) The abstract (p.1) and p.3 write 'Spearman's r2 = 0.36'; the analysis (p.8) reports a Spearman rank correlation of 0.36 and a Pearson r^2 of 0.26, so cite 'Spearman 0.36 (p = 0.03)'. (2) 'Up to 8%' is 8.0 percentage points (p.25). (3) The promised release date (June 2025) has passed and the text cannot say whether the release happened, so do not call GSM1k private without checking. (4) The sentence's other citation (Deng et al.) should carry 'leak'; GSM1k carries 'overfit'. (5) The authors caution that GSM8k and GSM1k are 'only highly similar, but not identically distributed' (p.4), and that providers receive the data by API (p.4). (6) Its related-work paragraph credits functional evaluations (Srivastava et al.) with ensuring that 'no datapoint is ever used twice', and claims for GSM1k the advantage that functional variants 'can only generate a tiny portion of the full problem space' by changing numerical values (p.3).
